title: Lifecycle Hooks: OnModuleInit, OnApplicationBootstrap, and Graceful Shutdown

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When a factory starts up, a checklist runs in order: turn on electricity (`onModuleInit`), connect to suppliers (`onApplicationBootstrap`), and open the front doors to customers (`listen`). When the factory closes, an exit checklist shuts off the machines gracefully without corrupting products (`beforeApplicationShutdown` / `onApplicationShutdown`).
progressiveExplaining.junior: NestJS providers and modules can hook into application startup and shutdown events by implementing lifecycle interfaces: `OnModuleInit` (called immediately after module dependencies resolve), `OnApplicationBootstrap` (called right before the app starts listening), `BeforeApplicationShutdown` (called when SIGTERM is received), and `OnApplicationShutdown` (called after connections close). To enable shutdown hooks, call `app.enableShutdownHooks()`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, lifecycle hooks provide deterministic initialization and cleanup ordering across the dependency graph. During startup, `onModuleInit` and `onApplicationBootstrap` execute in topological dependency order (deepest child dependencies first). During shutdown (e.g. Kubernetes pod termination via `SIGTERM`), NestJS pauses incoming HTTP requests, executes `beforeApplicationShutdown` to drain in-flight jobs, and closes database connections in reverse order, preventing connection leaks and half-written transactions.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: NestJS's `NestApplication` manages lifecycle stages. Startup iterates the `ModuleRef` dependency graph invoking `onModuleInit()` on all providers, followed by `onApplicationBootstrap()`. When `app.enableShutdownHooks()` is called, NestJS binds listeners to `process.on('SIGTERM')` and `SIGINT`. Upon signal receipt, it stops the underlying HTTP server (e.g. Express/Fastify `server.close()`), iterates providers invoking `beforeApplicationShutdown(signal)`, calls `onApplicationShutdown(signal)`, and exits the process cleanly.

codeComparison.title: Ad-hoc Process Signal Handlers vs Native NestJS Lifecycle Hooks
codeComparison.summary: Manual `process.on('SIGTERM')` handlers create race conditions with the HTTP server; NestJS lifecycle hooks ensure clean drained shutdowns.

legacyOrBad.label: Manual Process Listeners
legacyOrBad.snippet: process.on('SIGTERM', () => db.disconnect()); // ❌ Drops in-flight requests and causes race conditions

modernOrGood.label: Native NestJS Lifecycle Hooks
modernOrGood.snippet: export class DatabaseService implements OnModuleInit, OnApplicationShutdown { ... } // ✅ NEW

interviewGotchas.question: Why does `onApplicationShutdown` fail to fire on `SIGTERM` by default in NestJS?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your real-world production deployment experience on Kubernetes / Docker.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: By default, NestJS **does not enable system signal listeners** to save memory and avoid unintended process exits. You **must explicitly call `app.enableShutdownHooks()`** in `main.ts` before `app.listen()`. Without calling `enableShutdownHooks()`, receiving a `SIGTERM` signal (e.g. from Kubernetes during pod termination) will terminate the Node.js process immediately without running any `onApplicationShutdown` or `beforeApplicationShutdown` hooks.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Always call `app.enableShutdownHooks()` in production entrypoints to prevent database connection drop corruption during rolling deploys.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the execution order difference between `onModuleInit` and `onApplicationBootstrap`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of initialization phases in the NestJS container.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `onModuleInit()` runs for each module as soon as its individual dependencies are resolved (can be called while other sibling modules are still initializing). `onApplicationBootstrap()` runs **only after ALL modules in the entire application have finished their `onModuleInit`**, guaranteeing that all services across the entire dependency graph are fully ready.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not call cross-module dependent initialization logic in `onModuleInit()`; use `onApplicationBootstrap()` to ensure cross-module dependencies are initialized.
